name: US Coast Guard NAVCEN Space Operations Launch and Recovery (SOLAR) chart data file
robots: Allowed. robots.txt disallows only /core/, /profiles/, /admin/, /search/, /user/* etc.; /chart and /sites/default/files/tmp/test.js are not disallowed.
terms_or_licence: No site-specific terms page found. Works of the US federal government are not subject to US copyright (17 U.S.C. 105: 'Copyright protection under this title is not available for any work of the United States Government'). Treat as public-domain government data; still respect robots/rate limits. NAVCEN chart page has no footer terms/privacy link in fetched HTML. NOAA ENC base layer carries 'Not intended for actual navigation' disclaimer (SOLAR reference guide).
data_format: JavaScript file assigning a GeoJSON FeatureCollection: 'var chris = {"type":"FeatureCollection",...};'. Must be parsed as data (strip 'var chris =' and trailing ';'), never executed. 1295 features, all MultiPolygon, lon/lat order.
notes: Strongest free source found: official (USSF/USCG), mission-named, machine-readable polygons with Zulu windows, multi-family coverage and ~3 years of history in one file. Caveats: file path '/sites/default/files/tmp/test.js' looks unofficial/unstable; page banner says 'due to internal transitions, this page may not display all space operations missions currently active or planned' and points to https://navcen.uscg.gov/msi 'Space Operations' checkbox (not yet fetched). Epoch start/stop fields are unreliable; parse the Zulu text. Downrange box placement can indicate general direction (e.g. Bandwagon-1 downrange box ~30.35-32.45N 76-78W = NE; Bandwagon-3/4 ~27.4-28.2N 76-77.65W = ESE) but is not a route. Missions in the same series flew different directions.

name: NGA Maritime Safety Information broadcast warnings API (NAVAREA IV / HYDROLANT)
robots: robots.txt returns 404 (JSON body) - no robots restrictions published.
terms_or_licence: No site-specific terms page found. Works of the US federal government are not subject to US copyright (17 U.S.C. 105: 'Copyright protection under this title is not available for any work of the United States Government'). Treat as public-domain government data; still respect robots/rate limits. msi.nga.mil home is a JS SPA; no terms text retrieved.
data_format: JSON {'broadcast-warn': [...]} with msgYear, msgNumber, navArea ('4'=NAVAREA IV, 'A'=HYDROLANT, 'P','C','12'), subregion, text, status, issueDate, authority, cancelDate...; hazard areas are free text 'IN AREAS BOUND BY: A. 28-34.65N 080-34.37W, ...' (degrees-decimal minutes or DD-MM-SS).
notes: HTTP 200, but the public endpoint appears FROZEN: the newest message in any navArea of status=active is 101515Z MAY 2024, cancelled history ends May 2024, and no current Cape rocket warnings (CRS-35 launched 2026-10-13) are present. Even when live, warnings do not name the mission, so matching to a launch requires time-window correlation. Classified blocked_http because current data is unavailable via this endpoint; the format would otherwise be usable_hazard_corridor. Parameter filters status=all with msgYear return []; status=cancelled works. No API documentation found (/api/v3/api-docs 404).

name: Next Spaceflight launch pages
robots: robots.txt 404 (HTML 404 page) - no robots rules published.
terms_or_licence: No terms-of-use page found (/terms/ 404; footer links only About, Privacy Policy, Settings, Calendar, API Access). Privacy policy has no scraping/reuse clause. Footer: '(c) 2026, Next Spaceflight' - default copyright, no licence granted. /api_access/: 'We have been gathering feedback on offering a free, limited API for launch names and dates for community and personal projects. ... we currently don't have an ETA on when this may be available'. Reuse permission unresolved; contact owner before automated use.
data_format: Next.js server-rendered HTML; embedded RSC payload includes launch object with \"heading\":<int degrees>, \"net\", \"net_precision\", pad latitude/longitude, orbit. Visible text 'General Trajectory ... Launching Northeast|Southeast'.
notes: Technically extractable coarse heading for every family tested, but: (1) secondary aggregator, provenance of heading not stated; (2) values quantized to 45/135 so not a published azimuth; (3) no explicit reuse permission - treat as blocked for production until owner permission obtained; (4) a departure octant is not where a Maryland observer should look. Observed discrepancy: NSF lists Bandwagon-5 landing 'LZ-40' while SpaceX mission JSON says droneship 'A Shortfall of Gravitas ... stationed in the Atlantic Ocean'.

name: SpaceX website mission pages and content.spacex.com JSON
robots: www.spacex.com/robots.txt 404. content.spacex.com/robots.txt 200 with all rules commented out ('# User-Agent: *', '# Disallow: /') - no restrictions.
terms_or_licence: Not found: www.spacex.com/legal/ and /launches/ return the same 3134-byte JS shell (no terms text retrievable without JS); web search did not surface a SpaceX website terms page. Licence unknown; default copyright. Do not assume reuse rights.
data_format: JSON (Strapi CMS). launches-page-tiles/upcoming: title, link, vehicle, launchSite, launchDate, launchTime (local ET), returnSite, missionType, override.windowOpen/Close. missions/<link>: paragraphs (HTML), pre/postLaunchTimeline (T+ event times), infographic image URLs, flags toTheIssEnabled, vehicleTrackerEnabled, followDragonEnabled.
notes: No trajectory direction, azimuth, ground track text or coordinates in CRS-35 or Bandwagon-5 JSON. Event timeline gives T+ times only (no positions). CRS-35 'toTheIssEnabled': true implies ISS rendezvous (51.6 deg inclination) but direction is not stated. Infographics are generic landing graphics (F9_AUTONOMOUS_DRONESHIP, DRAGON_CARGO_LZ). /past endpoint 403.
